hypothesis: The serial coarse-root loop may leave cores idle when recursive shading workloads differ by tile. This candidate tests dynamic one-tile work assignment across root tiles, with run()'s thread count as the cap; the serial path is retained for one thread. It does not parallelize depth-bound rows, so its effect can be evaluated independently of that approach.
notes: Only the dynamic-schedule coarse-root experiment is proposed; no performance or correctness result is claimed. The controller should validate full output at 1 and 4 threads, including altered light colors, and compare measurements before drawing conclusions.
transformations: Pass run()'s thread count through to DispatchDynamicC and clamp the requested count to at least one.
Dynamically distribute independent coarse-root tiles in chunks of one when OpenMP is available and more than one thread is requested; preserve serial execution otherwise.
Leave depth-bound generation, higher tree levels, culling, and shading algorithms unchanged.
